clinician.trajectory_summary: A 5-year-old girl presented with a 3-month history of a transverse cutaneous 'split' on the plantar aspect of the right third toe with serous discharge that progressed circumferentially over 1 month. Physical examination revealed shortening of the distal phalanges of the 2nd, 4th, and 5th toes with normal sensation and pulses. Maternal history revealed similar transient demarcation lines on the 2nd, 4th, and 5th toes that resolved before toe shortening. X-ray imaging demonstrated complete resorption of the middle and terminal phalanx of the 5th toe, complete resorption of the terminal phalanx of the 4th toe, partial resorption of the terminal phalanx of the 3rd toe, and partial resorption of the middle and terminal phalanx of the 2nd toe. Comprehensive laboratory investigations including CBC, inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP), autoimmune panel (ANA, RF, anti-CCP), metabolic and endocrine studies (calcium, phosphate, PTH, thyroid function), and renal/hepatic function were all within normal ranges, effectively ruling out infectious osteomyelitis, connective tissue diseases, inflammatory arthropathies (including psoriatic arthritis), endocrine disorders, and lipid storage diseases. The diagnosis of idiopathic acral osteolysis was established based on the characteristic clinical presentation of transverse fibrous constricting bands with progressive osteolysis of multiple distal phalanges, supportive maternal history, and exclusion of secondary causes.
